 1           Plaintiff Dice Career Solutions, Inc. (“Plaintiff” or “Dice”) brings this action against

 2   Defendant IDC Technologies, Inc. (“Defendant” or “IDC”), and alleges as follows:

 3                                        NATURE OF THE ACTION

 4           1.      Defendant IDC failed to pay for the services that Plaintiff Dice provided to it. After
 5   letting the invoices pile up, IDC intentionally delayed and avoided providing Dice direct answers
 6   and information while Dice made good-faith efforts to establish a plan for the payment of IDC’s
 7   unpaid invoices. IDC now owes Dice $754,673.90, which IDC has not paid despite its contractual
 8   obligations and many promises. Therefore, Dice brings this action to seek recovery.
 9                                                   PARTIES
10           2.      Plaintiff Dice Career Solutions, Inc. is a Delaware corporation that has its principal
11   place of business located at 6465 South Greenwood Plaza, Suite 400, Centennial, CO 80111.
12           3.      Defendant IDC Technologies, Inc. is a California company with its principal place
13   of business located at 920 Hillview Court, Suite 250, Milpitas, California 95035.
14                                               JURISDICTION
15           4.      The Court has subject matter jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. §§ 1332 because there is a
16   complete diversity of citizenship, and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.
17           5.      This Court has personal jurisdiction over Defendant IDC because IDC has
18   deliberately engaged in significant and continuous business activities within this judicial district;
19   and resides in this district at its principal place of business in Milpitas, California.
20                                                    VENUE
21           6.      Venue is proper within this judicial district under 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) because IDC’s
22   principal place of business is situated in this district.
23                                       DIVISIONAL ASSIGNMENT
24           7.      Pursuant to Local Civil Rules 3-2(c), 3-2(e), and 3-5(b), assignment of the case to the
25   San Jose Division is proper because Defendant IDC has its principal place of business situated in
26   Milpitas, California, and a substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to the claim have
27   occurred within Santa Clara County, California.
28
                                                      1
                                                   COMPLAINT
              Case 3:25-cv-02196          Document 2      Filed 03/03/25      Page 3 of 7



 1                                       FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS

 2           8.      Plaintiff Dice provides AI-powered software products, online tools, and talent
 3   acquisition services to deliver a career marketplace where technology professionals can connect with
 4   potential employers. Dice has a long history of focusing on technology careers. Through its website
 5   Dice.com, Dice helps highly skilled technology professionals find employment opportunities to
 6   advance their careers, and enables recruiters and hiring managers to efficiently search, match, and
 7   connect with talent. Dice’s clients may purchase services individually or in bundled packages that
 8   include talent profiles, job postings, employer branding, and other services.
 9           9.      Defendant IDC is a Dice client and holds itself out as a provider of IT services and
10   staffing solutions for a variety of industries.
11           10.     On or around March 17, 2023, IDC and Dice entered into a Purchase Agreement for
12   a 24-month term beginning March 20, 2023 and ending March 19, 2025. A true and correct copy of
13   the Purchase Agreement is attached to the Complaint as Exhibit A.
14           11.     Under the Purchase Agreement, IDC agreed to pay a total of $1,549,348.00 in
15   exchange for Dice’s services, to be billed on a quarterly basis at an estimated amount of $193,668.50
16   each quarter for two years. The Purchase Agreement provides that in case of a breach of the
17   agreement, Dice may discontinue services and/or pursue all other available remedies to enforce the
18   agreement and obtain payment, and collect all of its costs and attorneys’ fees incurred.
19           12.     As of July 24, 2024, IDC owed Dice a total amount of $ 387,336.96 under the
20   Purchase Agreement.
21           13.     On July 25, 2024, an IDC employee emailed the Dice Account Manager responsible
22   for managing IDC’s account, and informed Dice that there was uncertainty about IDC’s ability to
23   pay its invoices. IDC could not promise Dice a definitive payment date but stated that it would try
24   to pay by August 25, 2024. IDC also requested a reduced monthly payment plan and asked that its
25   invoices not be sent to collections for payment. However, IDC did not pay its invoices by
26   August 25, 2024 as it said it would try to do.
27

28
                                                     2
                                                  COMPLAINT
              Case 3:25-cv-02196        Document 2       Filed 03/03/25     Page 4 of 7



 1          14.      On September 10, 2024, a Dice employee contacted IDC about the outstanding

 2   invoices. Namely, invoices for March, June, and September 2024—each for $193,668.48 and

 3   totaling $581,005.44—had not been paid. To find a solution, Dice proposed arranging a payment

 4   schedule beginning with an initial payment the following week, but IDC responded that funding

 5   would be delayed for a month.

 6          15.      IDC informed Dice that it expected to receive funding by the second week of October

 7   2024, and that upon receipt of the funding, IDC was planning to pay at least 50% of the March and

 8   June invoices immediately. On October 11, 2024, IDC released a payment to Dice in an amount of

 9   $20,000, but this was much less than what IDC had committed to paying, and still far short from the

10   total amount outstanding. Concerned by IDC’s failures to pay its invoices, Dice requested to speak

11   with IDC’s executive leadership to discuss the payment situation.

12          16.      On or around November 7, 2024, the parties had a phone call that included IDC’s

13   CEO, Prateek Gattani. An email memorializing the phone call summarized the outstanding 2024

14   invoices then due and the total amount that would be owed after accounting for the last quarterly

15   invoice in December 2024:

16          x     March: $173,668.48
17          x     June: $193,668.48
18          x     September: $193,668.48
19          x     December: $193,668.48
20          x     Total Amount: $754,673.90
21   During the November 7th phone call, IDC assured Dice that payment would be forthcoming.

22          17.      To date, IDC has not paid any of the total amount of $754,673.90 that is owed.

23   Throughout December 2024 and January 2025, Dice worked diligently to confirm a plan for

24   payment and made multiple demands for payment. However, IDC became increasingly

25   non-responsive and did not respond to multiple requests for information or meetings to discuss the

26   issue. Then, on January 30, 2025, IDC informed Dice that IDC was still in the process of securing

27   funds, and assured Dice that fulfilling IDC’s payment obligations was a top priority. The parties

28
                                                   3
                                                COMPLAINT
                Case 3:25-cv-02196       Document 2       Filed 03/03/25      Page 5 of 7



 1   agreed to have a phone call on February 7, 2025 to discuss the matter further with leadership, but

 2   IDC cancelled the meeting at the last minute, and has not responded to follow up messages.

 3             18.   Given IDC’s many repeated failures to pay, Dice has been left with no choice but to

 4   seek judicial relief for the collection of IDC’s unpaid debt totaling $754,673.90.

 5             19.   Under the Purchase Agreement, IDC agreed to pay for the services it was provided,

 6   and agreed that, in case of a breach of the Purchase Agreement, Dice would be entitled to pursue all

 7   remedies available for Dice to obtain payment under the Purchase Agreement.

 8             20.   The amount sought—$754,673.90—is the total balance that IDC owes under the

 9   Purchase Agreement. It is due and owing to Dice as of the date of this filing.

10                                      FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION

11                                           Breach of Contract
12             21.   Dice re-alleges and incorporates all of the preceding paragraphs as if fully set forth
13   herein.
14             22.   On or around March 17, 2023, Dice and IDC entered into a valid, enforceable
15   Purchase Agreement having a 24-month term. The Purchase Agreement expressly provided that IDC
16   would pay a total of $1,549,348.00 USD and would be billed on a quarterly basis at an estimated
17   amount of $193,668.50.
18             23.   Dice fully performed under the Purchase Agreement by providing services to IDC at
19   all times.
20             24.   By failing and refusing to pay no less than $754,673.90 in unpaid invoice amounts,
21   IDC breached the Purchase Agreement.
22             25.   As a direct and proximate cause of IDC’s breach, Dice has been injured and incurred
23   damages of at least $754,673.90.
24             26.   The amount that Dice seeks to recover for IDC’s breach of contract—$754,673.90—
25   is liquidated and certain.
26

27

28

                                                 COMPLAINT
                Case 3:25-cv-02196         Document 2        Filed 03/03/25      Page 6 of 7



 1                                      SECOND CAUSE OF ACTION

 2                                               Account Stated
 3             27.    Dice re-alleges and incorporates all of the preceding paragraphs as if fully set forth
 4   herein.
 5             28.    As provided for in the parties’ Purchase Agreement, Dice billed IDC on a quarterly
 6   basis for the services that Dice provided to IDC.
 7             29.    IDC did not object to the validity of the amounts stated in the invoices that it received
 8   from Dice, and accepted its account as correct.
 9             30.    IDC agreed to pay the amount owed under the Purchase Agreement on a quarterly
10   basis in amounts of approximately $193,668.50 each quarter.
11             31.    IDC has recognized its obligations to pay Dice the $754,673.90 total amount that
12   remains outstanding and owed to Dice under the Purchase Agreement.
13             32.    IDC’s account remains outstanding, and IDC is indebted to Dice in an amount no
14   less than $754,673.90.
15                               PRAYER FOR JUDGMENT AND RELIEF
16             Plaintiff Dice respectfully requests that the Court enter judgment against Defendant IDC and
17   in favor of Dice, and further requests that:
18             A.     The Court enter judgment that:
19                        a. IDC has breached its agreement with Dice by failing to pay Dice no less than
20                            $754,673.90 owed under the parties’ agreement; and
21                        b. IDC is indebted to Dice in an amount no less than $754,673.90.
22             B.     The Court enter an Order awarding damages in an amount of $754,673.90.
23             C.     The Court enter an Order awarding Dice its attorneys’ fees and costs for bringing this
24   action, as provided for in the parties’ agreement.
25             D.     The Court enter an Order awarding Dice pre-judgment and post-judgment interest.
26             E.     The Court enter such other relief as it deems proper and just.
27

28
